unresolved.finding: Command arguments are read into a fixed 100-character buffer without length or status handling, so longer arguments are silently truncated.
Unknown command-line options are silently ignored, and multiple informational options are all processed rather than terminating after the first recognized request.
Every return code after readinput is overwritten without inspection, so initialization, parameter lookup, step, output, or finalization failures cannot stop or alter the driver.
If either getdoubleparameter call fails, the ignored status leaves t or tstop potentially undefined before the main-loop comparison.
The main loop has no guard that executestep successfully advances t, so a failed or zero-timestep step can run forever because its status is ignored.

The XBeach grid branch decides whether a depth file is required from par%hotstart before the hotstart parameter is read from params.txt, so a requested hotstart can follow stale/default state and unnecessarily require or load depfile.

Critical positive quantities including dx, dy, dtheta, dtheta_s, tstop, gravity, and wave periods are read without strict=.true., so zero or negative out-of-range values only warn and can later drive divisions, invalid extents, or nonterminating angle normalization.
Delft3D mmax and nmax are converted directly to nx=mmax-1 and ny=nmax-1 without validating minimum or maximum grid sizes before downstream allocation and boundary indexing.
The dynamicroughness lookup embeds a trailing blank in the key literal, unlike the externally documented spelling and neighboring lookups, relying on blank-padding equality for recognition.
maxcf and mincf are read independently without enforcing mincf<=maxcf, permitting an inverted clamp interval.
The slopecorr parmapply call stores its selected option string into par%sedfricfac_str, overwriting the sediment-friction description instead of a slope-correction field.
morstart and morstop are bounded independently but never checked for morstop>=morstart, allowing an inverted morphology interval.
tint, tintg, tintp, tintm, and tinth use strict lower bounds of zero, allowing zero intervals that timestep_init later uses as divisors when generating schedules.
Every posdwn value below 0.1, including allowed small positive values, is coerced to -1 while other positive magnitudes remain unnormalized, making this nominal sign option behave discontinuously.
The tide auto-epsi branch tests epsi<-1 even though the configured default is exactly -1, so the documented automatic path is not entered at the default sentinel.
The warning text says wave-current interaction with non-stationary waves is experimental, but the condition emits it only for the stationary wave model.

Post-processing unconditionally reads tintg, tintp, tintm, tinth, wavint, morfac, morstart, morstop, and rt although several are assigned in all_input only under feature-specific branches, leaving correctness dependent on hidden defaults in the generated parameter declaration.

distribute_par broadcasts raw sizeof(par) bytes for a non-C-interoperable Fortran derived type containing pointer descriptors, copying process-local addresses and compiler-dependent representation across ranks before repairing only selected pointers.
The documented/default nglobalvar limit is 20, but the default global-output branch writes 21 names and sets nglobalvar=21, creating an inconsistent public count contract.

readOutputStrings searches parameter keys with exact case and without strippedline normalization even though the main readkey parser is case-insensitive, so inputs accepted for the count can fail when their following variable list is located.
Output-list and point-position readers open hard-coded unit 10 rather than obtaining a free unit, risking collision with another connected file.

readPointPosition searches indefinitely with external READ statements that have no iostat, so a missing or differently cased count keyword terminates on raw end-of-file instead of reporting a controlled input error.

When bcast is false, all scalar and vector readers assign results only on xmaster, so non-master callers receive undefined function results despite the routines remaining publicly callable on all ranks.
readkey_dbl parses through fixed F10.0 format, so only a ten-character field is consumed and longer valid floating-point values can be truncated or rejected.
readkey_str maps old option j to allowed(j) without requiring nov<=nv, while the independent allowed/old-name setup APIs permit more old names than allowed names.
The vector readers never require 0<=vlength<=tlength, directly section value_vec(1:vlength), and leave result elements vlength+1:tlength undefined.

Both vector readers handle only negative internal-read iostat, so a positive iostat from an invalid token is ignored and partially undefined elements are subsequently range-checked, logged, and returned.
readkey stores every line containing '=' into fixed 1024-element keyword/value arrays without checking ikey before incrementing, so a larger parameter file writes out of bounds.
The parameter cache is invalidated only when the filename string changes, so rereading a modified file under the same name returns stale values and stale used-key tracking.
readkey uses hard-coded unit 99 for both passes and does not check OPEN status, risking unit collisions and unstructured failures for inaccessible files.
parmapply assigns optional parm_str only on xmaster and never broadcasts it, so a present parm_str is undefined on non-master ranks even when parameter broadcasting is enabled.
parmapply indexes allowednames(idefname) without checking idefname against 1:numallowednames.
setallowednames tests only each optional name aN before dereferencing the independently optional value vN, so legal calls that omit a paired value reference an absent optional argument.
read_v_9 assumes optional outputs are present contiguously; presence of a higher-numbered argument causes all lower arguments to be read and broadcast even if some were omitted via keywords.
The read_v overloads perform external reads without iostat handling, so malformed or short records bypass the module's structured error reporting.
strippedline replaces every byte outside printable 7-bit ASCII with a blank, silently corrupting valid non-ASCII parameter values and filenames.
parameter pointer components have no default NULL() association, leaving unused components undefined or stale across descriptor reuse.

Every getkey result of a given type points to one module-saved scratch scalar, so a later call silently changes the value observed through all earlier descriptors and the routine is not reentrant or thread-safe.
Successful getkey calls set only name, rank, type, and one value pointer, leaving the public units, description, dimensions, and nonselected pointer fields undefined or inherited from a previous use.

arraytype's mutually exclusive pointer components have no default NULL() initialization, so newly declared descriptors contain undefined association status for every component not explicitly set by generated mapping code.
chartoindex reports an unknown name only by logging and returns -1 as an ordinary index, leaving callers able to subscript arrays with that invalid value.
dimensions is given both a DIMENSION(maxrank) attribute and an entity array specification (20), a duplicate shape declaration that standard-conforming Fortran rejects.
arrayf2c always returns c_loc(a) for a local three-element temporary rather than the requested farray storage, and that pointer becomes invalid when the function returns.
stringlength never exits on a null character and then unconditionally overwrites every detected position with size(char_array), so it always returns the full array size.
The collected and precollected flags have no default initialization in the type definition even though collection logic reads collected(index) to decide whether to skip work.
All exported computational range bounds lack initial values, so any use before ranges_init receives undefined indices.
index_allocate and index_allocated do not validate index as indextos does, and an invalid index can silently no-op or be reported allocated because the default result is true.
index_allocate unconditionally takes choice(1:1), which is invalid for a zero-length actual argument, and silently ignores nonempty unsupported choices.
space_distribute_vector treats every xy value other than lowercase 'x' as a y distribution, while space_distribute_block_vector accepts only lowercase 'y' and aborts for all other values.

The MPI decomposition subtracts fixed two-cell borders and immediately allocates local state without checking that every lm and ln is large enough, so an over-decomposed small grid can produce inverted computational ranges.
space_who_has returns the undocumented sentinel -123 when a point has no owning computational region and provides no status or diagnostic.
space_collect_index uses index directly in sg%collected before indextos can validate it, and space_collect_mnem passes through chartoindex results without checking for an unknown mnemonic.
For real rank-1 arrays and unsupported real ranks/types, space_collect_index performs no collection yet still marks sg%collected(index) true, suppressing future attempts.
gridprops assumes nx>=1 throughout and requires nx>=2 to define alfaz from an interior point; with nx=1 its two boundary-copy assignments merely circulate an uninitialized orientation.
gridprops inverts computed cell areas, and in 1D products of metrics, without rejecting zero-area or repeated-coordinate cells, producing infinite geometric factors.
ranges_init can produce lower bounds greater than upper bounds for small global or local nx/ny values, with no validation before those ranges are consumed by array sections and reductions.
posdwn is transformed to posdwn*abs(posdwn), so any value other than exactly -1, 0, or 1 unexpectedly rescales bathymetry rather than merely enforcing a sign convention.

For setbathy==1 the initial depth read is skipped, and for XBeach-format hotstart==1 it is also skipped, yet zb is sent, negated, boundary-copied, copied to zb0, and used for slopes before the later bathymetry/hotstart loaders define it.
The Delft3D comment-skip loop tests line(1:1) without first handling a nonzero read iostat, so EOF after comment lines can leave the previous '*' line in place and loop indefinitely.
The Delft3D branch skips the depth file for setbathy but not for hotstart, unlike the XBeach-format branch, causing a hotstart run to require and read a depth file that will be replaced.
Boundary copies assume nx>=1 and slope calculations divide by dsu/dnv without checking positive nonzero grid metrics.
dtheta and dtheta_s are used as divisors without validation and rounded counts can become zero, after which allocations and sigm=sum(...)/ntheta operate on an invalid or empty angular grid.

setbathy_init accepts nonpositive or unsorted nsetbathy/time values without validation, allowing an empty schedule to silently initialize every bathymetry value to zero or a nonmonotonic schedule to violate linear_interp's ordering contract.
wave_init allocates Dp, umwci, vmwci, zswci, and fw-related wave state but does not initialize Dp or the three WCI arrays before returning.
Wave intrinsic frequency is computed as 2*pi/Trep without a local positive-period guard for boundary types that do not force Trep to 10.
spectral_wave_init opens and reads the boundary file header without iostat handling, so missing or malformed input can fail outside the routine's structured logging path.

flow_init leaves several allocated arrays without initialization, including qmag, dUi, dVi, cfu, cfv, zs1, sigz, uz, vz, ustz, and nutz, creating an implicit requirement that every consumer wait for another producer.

Although hotstart zs, uu, and vv are deliberately preserved during allocation and initial zeroing, flow_init later unconditionally resets uu and vv and all derived flow quantities to zero, discarding the loaded hotstart velocities.
The hotstartflow fixed-point solver divides by s%cf immediately after flow_init explicitly sets s%cf to zero, and its convergence loop has no iteration cap or nonfinite-value exit.

For a completely wet domain under instant tide, the intended interpolation branch contains only comments and leaves both zs0fac weights zero everywhere, suppressing offshore and bay tide contributions.
sed_init returns with several allocated arrays uninitialized, including Tsg, vmag, vreps, vrepb, iwl, ccz, ca, and refA (and D15 when dilatancy is disabled).
Sediment layer assignments use nd_var and, in the single-grain case, forcibly set nd_var=2 without ensuring nd is at least two or that nd_var lies within 1:nd.
Multi-grain initialization normalizes any positive-sum fractions without rejecting individual negative fractions, so physically invalid negative bed composition can survive normalization.
For a line discharge classified in the v direction on a ny=0 grid, n1 is clamped down to zero and stored as a grid index.

Drifter positions are converted to integer indices by implicit truncation after metric division and are never clamped to the grid, so offsets outside the nearest cell or zero metrics can yield invalid indices.

All low-level hotstart readers capture open and per-row read iostat values but never test them, so fixed-format mismatches or I/O failures can silently leave restart arrays partially undefined despite the earlier list-directed length check.
timestep_init initializes the other counters and output flags but omits tpar%ith and tpar%outputh, which are subsequently read and incremented by outputtimes_update.
Generated schedules divide by wavint/tintg/tintp/tintm/tinth and allocate from the result without local checks for zero, negative, or otherwise invalid intervals and time ranges.
File-supplied schedule counts are read as real values, rounded with nint, and used as allocation extents without rejecting negative, nonintegral, or unreasonable counts.
All schedule files are opened on hard-coded unit 10 without checking whether that unit is already connected.

For duplicate scheduled times, each output counter advances only once while tnext excludes all times equal to the current time, leaving the counter pinned on the duplicate and preventing that output category from matching later times.

Current-output tests follow each array's counter order while next-time selection takes a masked minval over the full array, so unsorted file schedules can be stepped to without being emitted and counters can become permanently misaligned.

timestep's saved dtref has no explicit initial value and compute_dt initializes it only when it happens to equal zero or enters a t<=0 branch, making calls that begin at positive time depend on undefined saved state.
compute_dt returns before assigning present ierr or limtypeout when xcompute is false.

The cold-start timestep divides by sqrt(maxval(hh)*g) without a positive lower bound, despite the branch comment explicitly anticipating zero initialization, so an all-zero depth field yields an infinite or invalid timestep.

Several active stability expressions take square roots of hu/hv and divide by spacing-derived sums without guarding negative depths or zero cell metrics, allowing NaN or zero-division results to contaminate timestep selection.

In the 1D viscosity criterion mdx is a squared spacing but positive par%dy is assigned to mdy without squaring, unlike the 2D branch, producing a dimensionally inconsistent and incorrect stability limit.
Bed-celerity and sediment-diffusion reductions of par%dt do not update ilim, jlim, limtype, or dtold, so instability diagnostics can attribute the limiting timestep to an earlier criterion.
Groundwater stability calculations divide directly by par%kx and par%ky without local positivity checks when their respective branches are enabled.

The MPI path skips angular wave limiting when ntheta<=1, whereas the serial path applies it for every nonstationary model, potentially forcing a zero or spurious dt from a meaningless dtheta in the single-direction case.
timestep itself returns before defining a present INTENT(OUT) ierr when xcompute is false.
check_file_exist performs the inquiry only on xmaster without broadcasting error, so a present exist output is always reported true on non-master ranks regardless of the file's existence.

The three check_file_length variants do not validate extents or capture allocation/open errors, so bad dimensions or an inaccessible file can trigger a raw runtime failure before their intended read-error reporting.
checkbcfilelength does not assign filetype for wbctype values outside its enumerated branches, yet immediately selects on filetype, whose dummy argument has no declared intent or local default.
A LOCLIST file containing only its header produces nlocs=0 and skips all boundary-duration validation, allowing a positive-duration simulation to pass this check without any boundary file.

get_file_length opens hard-coded unit 11 without checking whether it is already connected, unlike the module's own free-unit allocator, risking interference with unrelated open files or an open failure.
get_file_length does not capture OPEN errors and treats every nonzero READ iostat as ordinary end-of-file, so malformed numeric input is silently reported as a shorter file.

create_new_fid_generic's initialized local tryunit has implicit SAVE and only decreases across calls, so closed units are never reconsidered and the allocator eventually reports exhaustion after enough cumulative opens even when nearly all units are free.
linear_interp_2d does not require nx and ny to be positive before applying reductions and using the resulting indices to access X, Y, and Z.
mkmap accepts n2 without validation but initializes search positions to one and calls hunt on zero-length arrays when n2 is zero, where hunt reads xx(n) and xx(1).
mkmap never initializes covered, so any target not processed as lying in a source cell retains undefined or caller-supplied status despite the documented default of zero.
make_map declares covered INTENT(OUT) but never initializes entries for targets not found in any source cell, leaving those output elements undefined.
Both mapping routines ignore bilin5's ier and copy hbuff even though bilin5 exits on several error paths without defining its INTENT(OUT) weight array, while also marking the target covered.
Both mapping routines explicitly round double-precision interpolation weights to real kind 4 before storing them back into double-precision w.

mkmap_step divides by dsu and dnv without zero checks and applies unrestricted floor offsets without ensuring the updated i1,j1 still identify a valid cell, so it can emit invalid flattened references.

grmap and grmap2 validate references only as positive (and grmap only gates on the first reference), so references greater than n1 directly index f1 and zero or negative later grmap references are silently redirected to f1(1).
ipon reduces translated double-precision polygon coordinates to real kind 4 before edge and crossing tests, making containment results lose precision and depend on absolute coordinate scale.
sort calls indexx for n=0, for which indexx reaches indx(0) and arrin(indx(0)) rather than returning on an empty input.
bilin5 leaves its INTENT(OUT) w array undefined whenever it returns ier=1, making even correct error-aware callers unable to rely on a deterministic failure value.
trapezoidal double-counts a full grid-cell contribution when both limits lie in the same cell or adjacent cells because Imid is formed even when there is no middle interval.
trapezoidal assumes n>=2, nonzero ascending spacing, ordered limits, and equidistance but validates none of these before division and index calculation.
trapezoidal_cyclic reads x(2), divides by dx, and indexes xp(1) and xp(np) without guarding n<2, zero spacing, reversed limits, or a resulting nonpositive np.
interp_using_trapez_rule unconditionally reads xtarg(2) and divides by the inferred spacing, so ntarg<2 or equal first targets cause bounds or divide-by-zero failures.
interp_in_cyclic_function's n>icycle+1 branch contains only a comment and leaves xc and yc uninitialized before they are used.
A zero, negative, or incompatible dx/xcycle can make icycle nonpositive, leading to invalid allocations and wrapping loops that cannot progress because they add or subtract icycle.

The interpolation fraction uses mod(xp,dx)/dx without subtracting the grid origin and uses sign-preserving mod for negative coordinates, so shifted grids or negative query coordinates can receive incorrect or extrapolative weights even though indices are cyclically wrapped.

fftn neither rejects nor reports zero, duplicate, or out-of-range dim entries (and silently truncates an oversized dim array), allowing invalid shape indexing, repeated transforms, or a zero-length normalization product.
fftradix returns for npass <= 1 without defining its INTENT(OUT) optional stat, after which fftn reads that undefined value when stat is present.
When a present dim array has size zero, fftn performs no fftradix call and returns without ever defining its INTENT(OUT) stat argument.
The products of caller-provided shape values are computed in default integer without validation, so nonpositive or overflowing extents can produce invalid scaling and assumed-size array traversal.
hilbert accepts m without validation, and m <= 0 reaches log(real(m)) and subsequent invalid exponent/allocation/index calculations.
hilbert declares xi complex but deliberately initializes the transform from only real(xi), silently discarding any input imaginary component without documenting that xi must represent real data.
hilbert computes both normalization factors through default-real real(n) and sqrt rather than fftkind precision.

flipa's flip==1 branch loops to M1 while indexing the second dimension temp3a(:,ii) and M1+1-ii, so a nonsquare M1-by-M2 array can be indexed out of bounds or only partly assigned and the branch does not actually reverse the first dimension.
random applies iabs to an unrestricted default integer seed, for which the most-negative representable integer is not representable after negation and can yield overflow or a nonpositive seed.
The POSIX usleep routine is declared as a C-interoperable subroutine even though the C API returns an integer status, so the binding does not match the external function's prototype.
myusleep does not reject negative durations and applies backend-dependent coercion, while the Intel/PGI paths also force zero or sub-millisecond requests to sleep at least one millisecond.
Saved allocation and `bccreated` state are initialized only for the first grid seen, with no reset or resizing contract for a later grid or reinitialization in the same process.
The TS readers accept `nt` without requiring it to be positive and then allocate from it and divide `sum(dataE)` by `nt`.
Several Surfbeat and nonhydrostatic boundary branches evaluate `par%t/par%taper` without the zero-taper guard used by the stationary branch, so an allowed zero taper can inject NaNs.
Bound-wave and nonhydrostatic formulas divide by boundary depth, `sinh(kh)`, `tanh(kh)`, and the resonant term `cg**2-g*h` without dry-point or small-denominator protection.
The spectral-record calculation divides by `dtbcfile` and derives direct-access record numbers from it without validating that this file-supplied interval is positive.

In the non-MPI multi-record-jump branch, both `q1` and `q2` are assigned from `gq2`, whereas the MPI branch distributes `gq1` into `q1`, eliminating the intended discharge interpolation only in serial runs.
The `par%order==3` branch contains only commented-out assignments, leaving `s%zi` and `s%ui` at prior or undefined values while execution continues as if a third-order boundary had been generated.
The difference-velocity rotation computes only `s%dUi`; `s%dVi` is neither replaced by the rotated transverse component nor included in the subsequent tapering.
The TS_NONH MPI path broadcasts several `isSet_*` flags but omits `isSet_V`, after which every rank branches on that uninitialized local flag.

When a TS_NONH file supplies discharge `Q`, conversion of `uig` and `duig` from discharge to velocity is compiled only in the non-MPI branch, so MPI runs distribute discharge values into velocity fields.

If a nonhydrostatic boundary file omits `Z`, `s%zi` is set to the absolute neighboring surface `s%zs(2,:)`, but the applied boundary later adds `s%zs0` to `s%zi`, apparently adding the mean level twice.

Flow-boundary work arrays are sized only on the first call, and `zs0old` is allocated only if the first call's tide type is instant or hybrid, leaving later dimension or tide-mode changes unsupported.
Hybrid averaging and relaxation divide by combinations of `cats`, `Trep`, and `hybtavg` without enforcing positive values.
All four hybrid minimum updates call `min` with the corresponding maximum accumulator instead of the previous minimum, so historical minima are lost whenever later samples rise.
Hybrid relative error divides by the maximum observed surface range without a positive floor, producing a zero denominator for constant-level windows.
Boundary mean velocities divide by globally accumulated metric lengths without checking for an empty or zero-width boundary selection.

Several absorbing-boundary formulas use unguarded water depths, group velocity, grid spacing, or angular denominators even though these branches do not consistently mask dry or degenerate boundary points.
Incident and reflected directions are obtained with one-argument `atan` of a quotient, losing quadrant information and becoming discontinuous near zero longitudinal velocity.
Back-boundary corner water levels use `dzs0dn(1,...)` and `zb(1,...)` instead of the `nx+1` back-boundary row, applying front-boundary geometry at both back corners.
Saved Coriolis parameter `fc` is initialized only when `par%t<=par%dt`, so a first call after that interval, such as a hot-start entry, uses an undefined value.
The lateral-boundary `select case` has no default assignment, so an unsupported `bctype` returns an undefined `vbc` vector.
Three lateral-boundary cases populate only indices `2:s%nx` before copying from indices 2 and `s%nx`, which leaves circular or undefined endpoint values when `s%nx<2`.

A horizontal discharge segment is considered local only when at least one endpoint lies in the rank's box, so a segment that crosses a subdomain while both endpoints lie outside that subdomain is omitted there.
Vertical point discharge clamps the global point into every rank's local index range without an ownership test, causing every MPI rank to apply the source at some local cell.
An unrecognized scalar/vector mode is silently accepted and leaves saved `lVaru` at its previous-file value.
Saved header indices are not reset when a new boundary file is initialized, so variables omitted by the new file can retain column indices from the previous file.

Although the header parser records the position of `T`, the data reader always consumes time as the first field and maps every other variable as column index minus one, making non-first time columns unsupported without validation.
Multi-character headers are matched against only selected capitalization variants, so otherwise accepted case variants such as `du`, `Dv`, or `DQ` can be silently ignored.
A one-record file sets `t1=t0` and duplicate timestamps are otherwise permitted, yet all initialized variables are interpolated by dividing by `t1-t0`.
Both end-of-file return paths assign only `isSet_Q`; the other `intent(out)` presence flags are left undefined even though callers immediately use them to accept or replace returned fields.
Unsupported wave-boundary combinations fall through empty branches without an error or deterministic reset, allowing boundary arrays to retain values from an earlier condition.
Final long-wave scaling is applied to the entire saved `s%ui` field rather than only the boundary row populated here, creating an unclear repeated-scaling contract for interior entries.
The `tideloc` and nested `paulrevere` selections have no default branches, so an unsupported value can leave the four module-level tide corner values unchanged from an earlier timestep.

Multiple tide gradients and spatial interpolants divide by grid spacing or endpoint-distance differences without guarding coincident points or zero spacing, allowing infinities or NaNs on degenerate grids or boundary placements.
In case 4, points beyond `distmaxzbl` receive the tide-2 water level but `tidegradient1`, making the reported gradient inconsistent with the selected side's forcing.
Water levels are clipped upward to the bed after gradients have been assigned, but the corresponding tide gradients are not recomputed or neutralized where clipping changes the surface.
The source explicitly states that `fill_tide_grid` is not fully MPI-compliant for distributed grids, while this routine supplies interior tide levels and gradients for instant and hybrid tide modes.
Boundary logic tests `par%ny` but indexes extents using `s%ny`, creating an unclear and potentially unsafe contract if parameter and allocated-grid dimensions ever differ.
Non-master ranks return before allocating tide arrays, and no distribution occurs in this routine.
For tideloc=0 the routine allocates a two-element tide time vector but returns without initializing it.
The counting pass treats malformed records as end-of-file and therefore silently truncates the tide series.
An empty tide file yields tidelen=0 and the duration check indexes tideinpt(0).
Non-master ranks return before allocating or initializing any wind fields, and this routine contains no distribution step.
All wind arrays are allocated unconditionally with no associated/allocated checks, requiring readwind to be called exactly once.
The record-count pass treats any nonzero IOSTAT as end-of-file, so a malformed record silently truncates the series rather than being reported.
An empty wind file produces windlen=0 and then indexes windinpt(0) in the duration check.
The purported next-generation boundary module exports nothing and contains no executable procedures because its only interface and implementation are entirely commented out.
randomseed is declared as a non-allocatable scalar, conflicting with wave_boundary_main's ALLOCATED and DEALLOCATE operations on that component.

Most administration scalars have no default initialization, so correctness depends on every entry path assigning them before use despite several consumers treating the datastore as persistent global state.
nspr is present in the procedure signature and used with PRESENT but has no declaration under implicit none.
After first initialization, changed np, coordinates, directional grid, boundary file, or reference/depth inputs are silently ignored with no invariant check.
MOD does not map negative angles into [0,2pi), contrary to the comment, so negative theta inputs remain negative.
The allocatable randomseed vector is deallocated and then assigned the scalar randomseed without allocating or constructing a conforming seed array.
isRecomputed is INTENT(OUT) but is assigned only when recomputation occurs, leaving it undefined on ordinary interpolation calls.
A single IF generates at most one series when t has advanced past multiple durations, so startComputeNewSeries can remain behind the requested time.
Energy interpolation slices eebct(i,itheta,:) even though generation stores it as (point,time,direction); this supplies a direction-length vector while passing the time-axis length.
The nonhydrostatic option still unconditionally interpolates hydrostatic eebct, qxbct, and qybct arrays that its generation path does not allocate.
lastwaveelevation is allocated but never initialized despite the stated zero-initialization intent, so the first taper can consume undefined values.
fid is assigned only under BUILDXBEACH although OPEN is unconditional, and err is tested in the LOCLIST counting loop before it is initialized.
The single-spectrum branch sets only local nspectra=1 and never stores waveSpectrumAdministration%nspectra, leaving the generator's spectrum count stale or undefined.
generate_wave_boundary_surfbeat assigns misspelled undeclared durantionlength and contains an unmatched endif, so the module cannot compile under implicit none.
The repeatwbc path skips initialization of local wp but returns wp%rtbc, and bccount is incremented only in a local copy rather than written back to waveSpectrumAdministration.
The instat select has no default, so an unsupported value leaves specin pointer components uninitialized before they are dereferenced.
generate_swts is called with two arguments even though its explicit module procedure accepts only wp.
Cleanup deallocates pointer-containing spectrum/vargen parents without deallocating their pointed-to arrays, leaking allocations on each generated series.
Zero-energy spectra and removed partitions reach unguarded divisions; in particular a zero scalefac1 can turn the overlap convergence metric into NaN and prevent its unbounded loop from terminating.
The SWAN reader notes non-monotonic frequencies but performs only no-op conversion before integration and 2-D interpolation assume ordered absolute frequencies.
SWAN and variance-density inputs index angle entries 1 and 2 without enforcing nang>=2.
When restoring a nonzero Sf into an empty interpolated bin, output-grid index i is used to index specin%S, which can exceed specin%nf and does not identify the corresponding input frequency.
The nonhydrostatic cutoff frequency omits the square root from the dispersion relation, yielding dimensionally incorrect filtering.
Without BUILDXBEACH the interpolation blocks are empty, leaving pdflocal and thetagen undefined while the routine continues to normalize and use them.
Simple-sum PDF normalization followed by trapezoidal CDF accumulation leaves the final CDF below one, so some random draws fall outside the interpolation range.
rtin is recorded as tslen*dtin although tin ends at (tslen-1)*dtin.
Variance is rescaled by (hm0/hm0post)^2 without guarding hm0post=0.
Spatial spectrum interpolation rescales by sfimp/sfnow without guarding sfnow=0.

Direction distribution allocates with uninitialized lntheta, uses uninitialized ldtheta, never allocates WDindex, indexes binedges with wave index i instead of itheta, and references undefined par_px.
BUILDXBEACH logging references s%ntheta and s%ny in generate_ebcf although no s object is in scope.
Inside the iy loop, scalar zeta(iy,...) values are assigned to the entire lastwaveelevation(:,itheta) column, so every boundary point is repeatedly overwritten with one point's elevation.
Each loop iteration assigns one scalar time to the entire internal tbc slice, leaving all finite time entries equal to the final loop value.
Interpolated samples use (it-1)*dtbc while storage time uses (it-2)*dtbc, and the no-interpolation whole-array assignment assumes tslen equals tslenbc although Kmin can make those extents differ.
generate_qbcf allocates q using s%ny even though no s object is declared or passed.
The per-point phase shift multiplies K-by-K matrices by whole npb-length distx/disty vectors instead of distx(j)/disty(j), producing nonconformable array expressions.
Hydrostatic output uses undeclared tslenbc, allocates qxbct twice, and never allocates qybct before writing it.
Flux interpolation repeats the one-step time offset, while direct assignments require q's tslen to conform to tslenbc.
Saved work arrays and cached scheme choices are initialized only once, requiring fixed grid dimensions, direction count, and schemes without enforcing that contract.
Mean wave directions use arithmetic angle averages and are incorrect for spectra crossing the angular wrap.
Wave-action conversion divides by sigm without a positive-frequency guard.
The breaking-model select omits BREAK_ROELVINK_DALY and has no default, so that configured model yields no breaking dissipation in this solver.
Directional dissipation omits Dveg despite other wave solvers including vegetation dissipation, an inconsistency explicitly noted in the source.
The convergence maxval applies a full-row wete mask to a jmin_ee:jmax_ee slice, which is nonconformable whenever those MPI bounds exclude halo columns.
The temporal smoothing factor is not clamped to [0,1], so sufficiently large dt relative to wavint or cats*Trep gives a negative weight to the previous state.
All slope differences divide by metric distances without guarding zero or invalid grid spacing.
Second-order theta advection is enabled for any ntheta>1, but ntheta=2 makes the boundary stencil reference ee(:,:,3) outside the two-bin array.
Second-order y advection with ny=1 can evaluate the left-boundary negative-velocity stencil at j+2=3 although the y extent is only 2.
Multiple saved/pointer work arrays are allocated once without later shape or option checks, creating undocumented fixed-grid and fixed-WCI configuration lifetime requirements.

iteratedispersion can never return its documented negative nonconvergence signal because the loop cannot leave with iter>itermax while the test accepts every iter<=itermax, including exhaustion at 150.
For ny=1 the breaker-delay computation loop is empty, so usd is not computed from current roller transport before lateral boundary copies use it.
An unsupported useAverageDepthSwitch leaves hhlocal and potentially velocities at stale values and continues the dispersion calculation.
The current-interaction taper can become negative when depth exceeds hwcimax because it lacks a zero lower clamp, reversing the current contribution to intrinsic frequency and group velocity.
compute_wave_direction_velocities has no default flavour case, so an invalid flavour leaves nthetalocal undefined.
Fy remains unset on several boundaries, as the code comments acknowledge, with lateral copies commented out and only selected MPI-edge rows assigned.
Stokes and roller fluxes divide wet-cell energy by c and hstokes without lower bounds, so zero phase speed or zero hstokes yields invalid fluxes.
Saved workspaces are never resized and mask_ee is only set true over the current interior without being reset, imposing fixed grid/decomposition bounds across the process lifetime.
For multi-directional waves the mean angle is an arithmetic weighted average, producing incorrect directions across the angular wrap.
The Snell branch clamps the asin input but still divides by coffshore without guarding a zero offshore phase speed.
Wave action conversion divides wet-cell energy by sigt with no positive-frequency guard.
Roller dissipation divides by sqrt(cx^2+cy^2) without guarding zero propagation speed.

Wave-crest boundary interpolation constructs nx+3 point coordinate/value arrays but passes nx+1 as their length, truncating the final interior point and upper sentinel and changing the intended interpolation domain.
After roller directional energies are rescaled, s%R is limited directly against gammax*hhw, mixing energy and height units, and is not recomputed from the scaled rr field.
Saved work arrays and the cached advection scheme are initialized only once, imposing an undocumented invariant that grid dimensions and relevant scheme settings never change.
Mean wave directions are arithmetic angle averages and therefore fail for energy distributed across the angular wrap.
The Snell-law asin argument is not clamped and divides by c(1,1) without a zero guard.
The x-advection timestep denominator uses maxval(cgx) rather than maxval(abs(cgx)), so an all-negative x velocity field selects the 1e-10 floor and an excessively large timestep.
Wave-action conversion divides by sigt without guarding zero intrinsic frequency.
The depth-limited breaking rescale divides by gammax*s%hh without a wet mask or positive-depth guard.
Roller source and dissipation updates divide twice by sqrt(cx^2+cy^2) without guarding zero propagation speed.
Fy is assigned only on interior i rows and j=1:ny, while its offshore/onshore and final lateral boundary rows are explicitly left unset by commented-out boundary copies.
Wave and roller mass-flux expressions divide by sigm without a lower bound, allowing infinities in zero-frequency cells.
callType has no default validation and saved work arrays are sized only on the first call, so a later call with a different grid or ntheta_local reuses incompatible shapes.
Mean wave direction is calculated as an arithmetic weighted mean of angles, which gives a direction near zero for energy straddling the -pi/+pi wrap instead of the correct circular mean.
The Snell-law asin argument sines times c/c(1,1) is neither denominator-guarded nor clamped to [-1,1], allowing division by zero or NaN directions.
Wave action conversion divides wet-cell energy by sigm without any positive-frequency guard.
Roller dissipation divides by sqrt(cx^2+cy^2) without guarding zero propagation speed.
After scaling directional roller energy by gammafac squared, s%R is assigned RH*gammafac, a wave-height quantity, instead of a consistently scaled roller energy.
Relative height convergence divides by s%H with no zero guard, while the EE branches populate wetmask but never apply it and therefore do not implement their apparent wet-cell-only contract.
The saved gamma workspace is allocated only once and never checked against later grid dimensions, leaving an undocumented fixed-grid-size lifetime contract.
Although hhw is protected against dry or negative depth, gamma is computed with the unclamped s%hh, so zero-depth cells can produce infinities or NaNs in hstokes.
The wavemodel select has no default case, so an unsupported value silently performs no wave update.

Master-only input populates testc, dimensions, switches, factors, and spectrum arrays while all corresponding broadcasts are commented out, leaving non-master ranks to branch on uninitialized values, allocate with undefined extents, and compute from undefined data.
The close(74) intended for the final timestep is unreachable after return, leaving a FILELIST unit open.
The ny>0 branch uses slices 2:ny, so ny=1 produces empty sums and division by zero instead of using the single offshore point.
An unsupported wbctype silently skips every spectrum builder but execution still advances list state and writes administration entries from stale or uninitialized wave parameters.
Zero wave height is accepted but multiple subsequent spectral normalizations and representative-period calculations divide by zero.
The SWAN frequency-conversion branch is a no-op and never repairs descending or relative-frequency input before moment integration and frequency-range calculations assume an increasing absolute axis.
The SWAN keyword-search loops have no I/O status checks, so malformed or truncated files can loop indefinitely or repeatedly read past EOF.
Both SWAN and variance-density readers dereference theta(2) without validating ndir>=2.
If the selected frequency range has one bin, M or wp%K can be one and the code divides by M, wp%K-1, and the resulting zero df.
The directional CDF starts above zero; a random draw below P(1) is extrapolated below theta(1), after which stepang can become zero and index S_array at column 0.
Nbin is never initialized and directions equal to the upper bin edge or still outside the opposite edge after wrapping receive no assignment before maxval and array indexing use.

The total envelope and directional weights are computed inside the directional-bin loop before later bins' zeta values exist, so Ampzeta for early bins depends on processing order and omits later directional components.
The standard-deviation denominators use size(array-1), which equals N rather than the apparently intended N-1.
Bound-wave direction uses atan(KKy/KKx) rather than atan2, losing the quadrant whenever KKx is negative.
Curvilinear flux rotation derives direction with atan(qy/max(qx,eps)), which clamps negative qx and cannot preserve the correct quadrant.
The routine increments bccount before the final-timestep early return, and that return leaves the INTENT(OUT) curline unassigned while also consuming a boundary-condition sequence number.

The external-time catch-up loop can call read_spectrum_input repeatedly on the same specin element, but each reader unconditionally allocates already-associated pointer components, causing an allocation failure when more than one spectrum interval is skipped.
The WBCTYPE select has no default case, so an unsupported value returns with specin uninitialized and later code dereferences its pointer components.
Hm0=0 is explicitly accepted, but the resulting zero spectrum reaches unguarded normalizations and weighted means whose denominators are zero.

The SWAN reader acknowledges that frequencies are often non-monotone but performs only no-op assignments, after which interpolation and integration assume ordered endpoints and can reject or negatively integrate a descending frequency axis.
Both spectrum readers index angular entries 1 and 2 without enforcing nang>=2, so a one-direction input can read out of bounds.
The nonhydrostatic cutoff frequency is computed as g*k*tanh(kh)/(2*pi), omitting the square root required by the dispersion relation and yielding dimensionally incorrect frequency filtering.

The PDF is normalized by its simple sum but its CDF is then formed with trapezoidal half-endpoint weights, leaving the last CDF value below one and sending some uniform random draws outside the CDF interpolation range.
tpDcalc divides by unguarded spectral moments, so an empty threshold mask or zero-energy spectrum produces an undefined representative period.
rtin is stored as tslen*dtin although the generated tin axis ends at (tslen-1)*dtin, creating a one-step inconsistency in the internal duration.
Wave-train variance rescales by (hm0/hm0post)^2 without guarding hm0post=0, which occurs when the selected component frequency range contains no energy for a location.
Spatial spectrum interpolation rescales by sfimp/sfnow without guarding sfnow=0.
wp%PRindex is allocated inside the offshore-point loop, so the second iteration attempts to allocate an already-associated pointer.

Cleanup deallocates pointer-containing parents without freeing their pointed-to Sf arrays and never deallocates vits, duits, or dvits, leaking substantial memory on each regenerated boundary condition.

When time-step interpolation is active, qinterp has only three fields and the writer omits the fourth elevation field even though the direct-access record length and non-interpolated path use four fields.

Allocation of six-field 3D arrays requires nonhq3d==1 and nhlay>0, but later use tests only nonhq3d==1, so nonhq3d==1 with nhlay<=0 accesses unallocated qx/qy arrays and fields 5-6 of four-field arrays.

Second-order component phases use Findex(1)+ii rather than Findex(1)+ii-1 (or Findex(ii)), shifting every primary component by one frequency bin and reading beyond the generated-component span for ii=K.
The high-wavenumber cutoff tests only k3(m,1), but rows m>K+1 populate columns ii>1 while column 1 remains zero, so those higher rows evade the cutoff.
The upper-layer qx2/qy2 ratios subtract sinh(KKx) or sinh(KKy) with no depth factor, unlike the surrounding dimensionless sinh(k*depth) terms, producing dimensionally inconsistent layer partitioning.

The 3D second-order update divides the first-layer flux by z (negative) and the second by h0+z, inconsistent with the layer thicknesses and with the earlier short-wave implementation that uses h0+z for layer 1 and -z for layer 2.
Second-order 3D generation computes qy1 and qy2 fields but the accumulation branch updates only uits and duits, leaving vits and dvits without the corresponding transverse second-order contribution.
The second-order interpolated q-file path repeats the three-field qinterp versus four-field record mismatch, omitting elevation when dtchanged is true.
Pointer components have no default NULL initialization, yet ASSOCIATED is called on fobs1 before any guaranteed association-status definition.
bwinit unconditionally allocates eight space-state arrays and provides no deallocation or already-allocated guard, so a repeated initialization fails.
Saved Beach Wizard arrays are allocated only on first use and never resized or released, making reuse with a different grid shape unsafe.
Only bwinit is explicitly master-only while assimilation and update routines have no matching rank guard, leaving non-master allocation and state-update requirements unclear.
When bwdefaults.inp is absent only scalar defaults are set, not the allocated sig arrays, and sigS is subsequently used even when no shoreline source caused it to be filled.
The uncertainty-map read path is entirely commented out and statuserr therefore remains zero, so configured fnameerr files are silently ignored.
The image schedule count is not constrained to the 1000-row arrays, and the time-advance loop can read itimnew+1 beyond the final slot.
A missing assimilation information file executes STOP inside library code rather than returning a diagnosable error to the caller.
Header-read errors jump past CLOSE, potentially leaking unit 31 and leaving partially replaced observation state.
Observation-grid dimensions and spacings are used for allocation, division, MOD, and indices that assume nx and ny are at least three without validating positive dx, dy, nx, or ny.
All model points outside the observation footprint are clamped to an interior observation cell rather than marked missing, causing implicit constant extrapolation over the entire model domain.
The wavenumber source is copied into cobs instead of kobs, after which uninitialized kobs values drive the celerity residual and uncertainty calculations.
Celerity and wavenumber calculations divide by unchecked tradar, hh, rk, and rk plus sigK and are evaluated over dry cells before any wet-cell guard.
The celerity formula adds dimensional Hrms directly to dimensionless rk times hh inside TANH, indicating an inconsistent or mistranscribed dispersion expression.

Bathymetry, celerity, and wavenumber observations are read or converted, but the final observation variance and depth correction combine only dissipation and shoreline terms, so those advertised sources cannot affect assimilation.
The backward-distance loop divides by an unchecked average wavelength and has no progress guard, so zero or nonpositive dsc or L1 can make disfac invalid or leave backdis unchanged indefinitely.
For ny equal to zero the h2 loop is empty and the subsequent assignments reference columns 2 and 0 of a one-column allocation.
Hb and dHbdh divide by k and by sinh(kh) times cosh(kh) plus kh without protecting the common zero-k or zero-kh limit.
Assimilation divides by Trep, dt, and tstop without requiring these time parameters to be positive and nonzero.
The weighting and depth-correction formulas lack guards for zero combined variance and for the all-zero dDdh case, where the latter evaluates an explicit zero-over-zero.
The dissipation-derived depth change is capped before the shoreline correction is added, allowing the final dassim applied to the bed to bypass the stated ten-percent depth limit.
Local allocatable work arrays are tested for allocation and allocated on every call but automatically deallocate on return, making the guard ineffective and imposing repeated large allocation cost.
Both bed-friction select blocks lack a default branch, so an unsupported selector leaves cfu and cfv unchanged or uninitialized without reporting an error.

Saved work arrays are allocated without a module teardown or shape check, and several initialization allocations are unguarded, so repeated initialization or reuse at another grid size can fail or retain incompatible storage.

Chezy and White-Colebrook formulas divide by unchecked bed-friction or roughness coefficients and take logarithms derived from them, allowing zero or nonpositive input to produce invalid coefficients.
Dynamic Manning roughness divides by dstem and droot without requiring either configured length scale to be nonzero.
Update-time friction omits the initialization-time mincf lower clamp, and the grain-size u branch uniquely hard-caps at 0.1 instead of maxcf, producing direction- and timestep-dependent bounds.
The infiltration enhancement divides by cfu or cfv twice without a positive lower-bound guard, which is unsafe for zero-valued constant-friction configurations.
Exactly zero infiltration is forced to a nonzero negative blphi and therefore a facbl slightly different from one, so the nominally absent process still adds shear.
Acceleration models divide by Trep-derived smoothing and frequency scales and by saved dt without validating Trep and dt as positive.

The two acceleration implementations use the same allocation sentinel but allocate different array sets and initialize phirad only in one branch, so changing implementations during a process can expose unallocated or uninitialized saved state.
Using SIGN with zero velocity assigns positive turbulent bed shear at rest, introducing a fixed directional bias wherever kbl is positive.
The saved Fi array is allocated but never read or written after allocation.
Drifter displacement divides directly by local dsu and dnv without validating that either grid spacing is positive and nonzero.

Every rank whose local index test succeeds advances the drifter, while idrift and jdrift are reduced independently with MPI_MIN, so overlapping ownership or differing local updates can select coordinates from different ranks and create a position no rank computed.
Strict start and end comparisons skip updates exactly at both configured activation times, leaving the endpoint semantics unclear and potentially losing a timestep.
Module-global work arrays are allocated only once and have no resize or teardown path, so reuse with a different grid shape leaves an incompatible saved allocation.

Multiple two-dimensional correction formulas hard-code the transverse metric index to 1 even though neighboring code uses the current i or j, making the scheme inconsistent on spatially varying curvilinear grids.
The negative-v qy continuity branch omits the sign reversal used by the corresponding negative-u branch and by the other second-order flux routines, yielding a correction with the opposite sign.

The continuity correction is computed with fixed whole-array loops and then unconditionally zeroes every local outer work-array edge without MPI-aware exchange or boundary tests, so subdomain-interface corrections can be discarded and the update can depend on decomposition.

Old-state arrays are allocated only if second-order or nonhydrostatic mode is active on the first call, so enabling either mode later accesses unallocated storage; all saved work arrays also retain the first grid shape.
The viscosity-off branch clears nuh and viscu but not viscv, so a runtime transition from enabled to disabled viscosity leaves the prior V-viscous acceleration active.
The Smagorinsky cross-stress mask for V momentum multiplies three wetu values but uses wetv(i-1,j) for the fourth point, inconsistent with the U-velocity stencil.
The physical left boundary passes par%right to flow_lat_bc while the physical right boundary passes par%left, an unexplained reversal of boundary configuration.

Multiple cell/face interpolants (vu, vsu, usu, uv, vsv, usv, ue, and ve) leave MPI-internal halo rows/columns or nx+1/ny+1 edges unset, as the inline comments acknowledge, yet whole-array velocity magnitudes consume them.
The vertical-profile call derives ks using sqrt(g/cfu) without ensuring positive cfu and passes potentially zero sigm/k values into a routine that divides by both.
The 2-D Smagorinsky stencil reads i±1 and j±1 at generic computational bounds under an explicit MPI-warning comment, without local bounds/halo validation.
gw_init allocates every groundwater field unconditionally and provides no already-allocated guard or cleanup for a second model initialization.

Saved solver and work arrays are allocated only for the first grid and first solver branch, so later changes in dimensions, dimensionality, fast-solve choice, or head model reuse incompatible storage/state.
Dynamic-pressure smoothing divides by Trep without validating a positive period.
Updated Kx, Ky, and Kz are all smoothed only along the i direction, even for the nominal y-direction conductivity Ky.
infilcon is first allocated its own target and later pointer-reassociated to s%infil, permanently losing the original allocation.
Several scheme/model SELECT CASE blocks have no default, so unsupported gwscheme or head-model values leave logicals or result/output variables undefined.
gwhu(nx+1,:) and gwhv(:,ny+1) are assigned only on physical bottom/right ranks, yet velocity and flux loops consume all nx+1 by ny+1 entries on internal MPI ranks.
The wet-layer ratio divides by dwetlayer with no positive-value guard.
The exponential head formulation repeatedly evaluates sinh(h)/h at cells whose groundwater height can be zero, without a limiting-form implementation or mask.
The fast 2-D parabolic solver loops on i but writes A and rhs at index k, which remains initialized to zero, causing second-dimension index-zero accesses.
The fast 2-D exponential solver loops on k but never sets i, so it uses stale/zero i to index all grid fields and metrics.
In the fast 2-D branch x(:,1) has nx+1 elements but is assigned to gwhead(2:nx,j), which has nx-1 elements.
The full 2-D branch builds and solves a matrix only for the parabolic model; selecting exponential skips the solve and then computes gwhead from stale gwcurv.
Critical groundwater velocity divides by D50(1) without validating a positive grain diameter.
Both v-interface infiltration calls pass Kx instead of Ky, and the first v-interface surface-water availability limit uses dsz where the surrounding v-direction scaling uses dnz.
Turbulent conductivity iterations have no iteration limit or non-finite/stagnation exit.
Local infiltration divides by dt, porosity, twodtp, dis, and infiltration rate without explicit guards, so zero conductivity or invalid timestep/porosity can cause singular intermediate arithmetic.
Many saved work arrays are allocated only on first use and never resized or reconfigured, so changed grid, grain, layer, or formulation settings in a later lifecycle retain incompatible state.
With nz>1, ueu_sed and veu_sed are filled only through nx, while whole-array velocity magnitudes immediately consume their nx+1 boundary; non-bottom MPI ranks do not initialize that boundary.
At the right MPI boundary, uev_sed(:,1:ny+1)=uev_sed(:,1:ny) assigns arrays with different extents instead of assigning only the final column.
The Surfbeat berm-slope mask evaluates H/hu across the full grid without a wet or positive-depth guard.
The bed-slope magnitude condition applies the non-berm mask only to the Svb alternative, so any nontrivial Sub is modified even where bermslopeindexbed is true.
Talmon direction calculations use atan of component ratios rather than atan2, including a possible zero denominator and loss of the correct quadrant for the adjusted transport direction.
pbbedu(nx+1,:) and pbbedv(:,ny+1) are never assigned before whole-array multiplication into Sub/Svb, so boundary transports can consume undefined values even when a zero transport is expected.
Concentration updates divide by Tsg, dt, and hh without explicit positivity checks at the addressed cells.
Groundwater coupling adds accretion exchange to infil as depth divided by dt, but erosion exchange is added without dividing by dt.
Avalanche erosion searches depth layers without an nd bound, and deposition multiplies edg2 by sedcal a second time, applying sedcal squared and potentially failing mass conservation.
D50top and D90top are assigned as whole arrays inside the i,j loops, so every iteration overwrites the entire field and the final cell's mixture becomes global.
update_fractions sizes scratch arrays from s%nd(1,1) but indexes them using each target cell's nd and par%nd_var, which can overrun when layer counts vary spatially.
The fraction update loops until a floating residual is exactly zero and can make zero progress when a limiting layer thickness is zero, with no tolerance or iteration cap.
Zero or invalid grain size/fall velocity can enter negative powers and divisions when computing Sster, ws, and adaptation time.
Bore turbulence divides by Tbore and the runup jet indexes nint(istruct) and divides by local hh without bounds or positive-value checks.
Suspended-load critical velocity uses Ucr*(1+sqrt(srfRhee)) while bed load uses Ucr*sqrt(1+srfRhee), an unexplained nonlinear inconsistency for the same Shields correction.
Van Rijn bed load gates on ue>Ucrb but then divides by used=vmg+ua, which can be zero or negative independently and produce invalid or sign-reversed concentration.
The concentration grid divides by kmax-1 and therefore requires kmax>=2 without checking that contract.
Nielsen2006 allocates fe only when streaming==1 but assigns fe=0 unconditionally, so streaming-disabled initialization accesses an unallocated allocatable array.
After the smoothing loop, both transport routines set the top boundary from qsedu(i,:) where loop variable i has advanced to nx+1, copying the opposite boundary rather than qsedu(1,:).
intra_sedtr defines ratio_s=(rhos-rho)/rho and then uses ratio_s-1 in dstar, subtracting unity twice relative to the submerged-density ratio used elsewhere.
ceqbg is formed by dividing bed transport by hh*uu before the low-shear mask is applied, and the bed-disabled branch clears Subg but not ceqbg.
The negative y-slope Nielsen branch tests dzbdx<0 instead of dzbdy<0, so many negative y slopes bypass correction.
Suspended concentration divides by hh-za and hh without ensuring water depth exceeds the reference height or is positive.
Bulk McCall-Van Rijn concentration divides qsedu by hu*uu over the whole grid, including dry faces and zero-flow wet faces.
At zero V velocity, kturbv is averaged from kturbv itself rather than from s%kturb, reusing stale work-array values instead of the neighboring turbulence field.
In 2-D turbulence advection, disturb is used after the betad<=0 branch where its only assignment is commented out.
Turbulence updates divide by hh over unmasked interior ranges, allowing dry cells to generate invalid values.
RvR forms the Ursell number with (k*hh)^3 in the denominator before applying a lower bound, so zero k or depth produces NaN that max does not neutralize.
vT computes H/hh, sqrt(g/hh), and related bore terms for every grid point without a wet mask, so dry cells can contaminate table indices and outputs.
Any ipredcor value other than zero silently selects the correction path, so an invalid selector is accepted as a valid corrector request.
The one-layer routines lazily initialize module storage, but the reduced two-layer predictor paths do not, leaving their correctness dependent on an undocumented external nonh_init call.
nonh_init allocates module arrays unconditionally and never supports cleanup, resizing, or changing nonhq3d mode during a later model lifecycle.
The original formulation constructs reciprocal grid spacings without checking for zero or invalid ds/dn metrics.

Several one-layer pressure, advection, viscosity, and explicit-pressure terms divide by hh based on nonhZ rather than an explicit positive-depth check, relying on the mask contract to guarantee a safe depth.
In the 1-D excluded-point bottom boundary calculation, dzb_w is assigned dzs_e instead of dzb_e, mixing free-surface and bed slopes.
In the 2-D excluded-point surface condition, the both-wet V branch assigns dzs_n=dzb_s rather than dzs_s, injecting a bed-slope value into the surface condition.
In the 2-D excluded-point bottom condition, the both-wet U branch assigns dzb_w=dzs_e rather than dzb_e.
The y-direction vertical-viscosity flux uses s%hu at lines 1174-1175 even though it is evaluated across V faces, unlike the expected y-face depth s%hv.
Both reduced correctors claim to recalculate zsu/zsv/zbu/zbv but contain no zuzv call, so matrix and kinematic corrections use geometry last computed in the predictor.
Reduced-layer formulas divide by 1-wcoef, 2-wcoef sums, and nhlay-nhlay^2 while only checking nhlay>0, so nhlay/wcoef equal or near one makes the system singular.
The xmpi_isleft branch assigns Wm(1,:) instead of Wm(:,1), overwriting the top x row and leaving the left y boundary unset.
The 3-D U-pressure east coefficient uses wcoef(i,j) for the i+1 cell, inconsistent with its hh(i+1,j), the 2-DV implementation, and the analogous V coefficient.
The dV pressure correction forms surface and wcoef differences as current-minus-next while dU uses next-minus-current, despite the base U/V pressure gradients sharing the same orientation.
The dV bottom-friction update uses s%cfu rather than the V-face friction coefficient and averages wcoef across i/i+1 rather than j/j+1.
wcoef initialization does not validate Topt, and disper has singular arithmetic for zero frequency/depth plus an iteration with no maximum-count or stagnation guard.
On non-bottom MPI ranks zbu(nx+1,:) and zsu(nx+1,:) are not assigned or exchanged by zuzv, although nonh mask construction iterates through nx+1 and reads zbu there.
Only the master initializes constantRainfall, and workers receive it only when the first update satisfies t<=dt, so restart or nonstandard first-call timing can leave the worker flag undefined.
rainfall_init allocates all rainfall arrays unconditionally and provides no cleanup or already-allocated guard for a second initialization.
The file-driven path passes nrainfallrate and timestamps directly to LINEAR_INTERP without checking that at least the required number of records exists or that times are ordered.
Saved scratch arrays in all formulations are allocated only once and never resized, so reuse with a different grid shape has stale bounds.
Roelvink breaking computes H divided by depth-dependent limits over unmasked arrays, so zero-depth cells can evaluate 0/0 and contaminate Qb.
The Daly branch updates Qb only at wet cells but then computes D for the full addressed row/domain, leaving dry-cell Qb and potentially D dependent on prior state.
BREAK_ROELVINK2 and Daly scale dissipation by H/hh without a wet mask or positive-depth guard.
Frequency conversions divide by par%px or par%Trep without local validation of the required positive-period contract.
Janssen-Battjes divides directly by k when forming Hb and by hh when forming D, unlike the guarded k division in Baldock, so calm or dry points can generate infinities/NaNs.
dx and dy accept zero even though they define ship-grid coordinates and the area supplied to grmap2, allowing a degenerate mapping grid.
When heading is derived, the code unconditionally accesses track samples 1 and 2 (and the final sample's predecessor), so a track with fewer than two records is out of bounds.
For compute_motion=1, zhull is allocated but not initialized before it is used to compute pressure and force; the hull geometry update occurs only afterward.
shipphi, shipchi, and shippsi are allocated without initialization, while shipphi and shipchi are consumed during the first motion-enabled hull update.
Heading is linearly interpolated as an ordinary scalar after conversion to radians, with no unwrap handling for tracks that cross the 0/360-degree discontinuity.
The saved firstship flag is never reset by ship_init, so a second model lifecycle in the same process will skip its initial water-level adjustment.
Integer division nx/2 and ny/2 makes odd-sized ship grids asymmetric about the declared center of gravity.
World-coordinate ship-grid positions are combined with ship-local xCG/yCG when computing hull rotations and roll/pitch moments, making results depend on the global coordinate origin.
For motion-enabled ships, pressure forces are computed from the previous hull position and only then is zhull updated, creating a one-step geometry/force lag even after initialization.
Vertical force uses only ph(ix,iy) per panel while horizontal forces average edge pressures, introducing a directional inconsistency in pressure integration.
itmin starts at zero and is updated with min(it,itmin), so its reported minimum can never become a positive observed iteration count.
solver_init marks the module initialized even when par%solver matches neither supported branch, after which solver_solvemat silently performs no solve.
solver_free deallocates the work arrays but does not reset initialized, so a subsequent solve skips reinitialization and accesses unallocated residual/work storage.
Solver settings and array dimensions are captured only on the first initialization, with no protection against a later call using changed nx, ny, solver choice, or solver parameters.
The Thomas solver divides by each pivot while the normal caller omits fixshallow, so zero or near-zero pivots are not guarded.
For bnorm=0 the convergence threshold is exactly zero and the strict rnorm<epslin test can never pass even for an exact zero residual, forcing maxit iterations and recording nonconvergence.
SIP divides by 1+p1, 1+p2, and p3 without finite/near-zero checks; adding a fixed 1e-15 only to p3 does not protect the first two denominators or scale with the matrix.
Species-name reads record iostat in ier but never inspect it, so a short or malformed species list can leave names undefined and fail later in a misleading way.
Spatial vegtype values are never checked against 0..par%nveg before being used as veg(ind), so an oversized map value causes out-of-bounds species access.

swvegatt treats each ahveg value as a thickness by adding ahtold, while momeqveg treats it as an absolute section height and only stores ahtold afterward, producing inconsistent layer geometry for multi-section vegetation.
Saved totT is initialized only when floating-point par%dt exactly equals par%t; otherwise its first comparison is undefined and can lead to use of unallocated unl/etaw arrays.
Several saved allocatable work arrays are allocated only once and never resized, so reuse with a changed grid shape retains incompatible bounds.
When a vegetation section lies wholly above the wave crest, FvgCau and FvgCav are not reset, yet vegcanflo can still add their values from a preceding section or cell.
Nonlinear and canopy-wave forces divide by s%hh for every vegetated cell without a wet-cell guard, so dry vegetated points can generate division-by-zero or NaN values.
swvegnonlin divides by s%hh and takes sqrt(g/s%hh) over the entire grid with no wet mask, making zero-depth cells feed infinities/NaNs into table interpolation and output profiles.
bulkdragcoeff divides by sigm, hh, sinh(k*hh), bveg, and alfav powers without guarding calm, dry, zero-height, or zero-width cases.
porcanflow deliberately leaves Fcanu/Fcanv unchanged in non-canopy cells, so any runtime change from canopy to non-canopy would retain the prior canopy force.
delta is assigned only when omega>0 but is used unconditionally at line 86, so a zero/nonpositive omega path consumes an undefined value.
cw=omega/k is formed without guarding k, and several later divisions by omega or cw occur even though the preceding branch explicitly permits cw<=0.
The first nonlinear iteration computes tbnw from dhdx and dhdy before either local variable has been initialized.

Derived denominators and logarithm arguments involving sigmas, sigs1, delta, and sigma0 are used without validating their ordering or separation, allowing singular or invalid evaluations for admissible-looking shallow/rough inputs.
Failure of a local profile iteration terminates the entire process with STOP instead of returning a recoverable status to this library routine's caller.
The implementation requires n>=2 (division by n-1 and references to sigz(2) and sigz(n-1)) but neither checks nor documents that precondition in the interface.
The Rouse-profile expression is evaluated at sigz(n)=1 with a zero denominator whenever ast<1, relying on divide-by-zero/infinity behavior before the resulting endpoint weight is summed.
The internal stokes routine lacks IMPLICIT NONE and INTENT declarations, weakening compile-time detection of misspelled locals or unintended argument modification.
The saved work array weteb is allocated only on the first call and is never resized, so a later call with different s%nx/s%ny would use stale bounds.
The source explicitly notes that boundary hu/hum and hv/hvm values require MPI neighbor communication, but no communication is performed here before those values drive wet/dry masks.
MPI return codes from communicator, datatype, collective, point-to-point, and free operations are never checked.
A root-contract violation aborts MPI_COMM_WORLD rather than the communicator supplied by the caller.
Vector distribution creates subarray datatypes from unchecked is/lm metadata and destination extent, permitting invalid starts or subsizes.
Block-vector distribution independently uses size(a,2) for send types and size(b,2) for receive types without verifying equality, so sender and receiver type signatures can disagree.
All matrix distribution and collection implementations depend on genmpi_distr.inc and genmpi_coll.inc, but neither include exists under source_code.
decomp divides and takes modulo by numprocs without rejecting zero and does not validate myid.
det_submatrices assumes output arrays have at least mp*np elements and dimensions exceed the fixed four-cell overlap without validating either condition.
Border shifting indexes second and penultimate rows/columns and uses ma-2 counts without checking minimum matrix dimensions.
MPI status codes are consistently captured but not checked, so communication failures can leave partially populated arrays or enter later waits with invalid requests.
Vector distribution indexes is/lm by communicator size and copies lm elements into b without validating metadata extents, source ranges, or destination capacity.
Scatter variants trust is/lm/js/ln and local matrix shapes completely, allowing invalid displacements, counts, or b columns to be passed to MPI.
Both column-send root loops terminate only after incrementing sends, so a valid zero-total workload makes the unbounded loop advance j forever.
The send variants allocate a full bb copy on the root even though bb is only read on non-root processes.
Whole-matrix distribution computes array sections from unchecked metadata and root rank before validating that source and destination shapes match.
Shape mismatches abort MPI_COMM_WORLD rather than the communicator passed to the routine, unexpectedly terminating unrelated ranks in an embedded or split-communicator use.

Column collection derives counts, receive totals, and array sections from unchecked overlap flags and metadata, so inconsistent flags can produce negative counts, missing receives, or out-of-bounds sections.
Whole-submatrix collectors subtract a fixed four-cell overlap without enforcing local dimensions of at least four, allowing negative extents and MPI counts.
decomp divides and takes modulo by numprocs without rejecting zero, and does not validate myid against the process range.
det_submatrices assumes all eight output arrays contain at least mp*np elements and that ma/na exceed the fixed overlap, but validates neither condition.
Border shifting forms rows/columns 2 and ma-1/na-1 and uses count ma-2 without checking that the matrix has sufficient dimensions.
getparametertype_c always returns success zero and does not validate the index returned by getkey_indextype, so an unknown parameter can return an undefined type code as a successful query.
Several Fortran wrappers assign the fixed 1024-element result of string_to_char_array into automatic arrays sized only len(name) or len(name)+1, which is a nonconforming whole-array assignment.
Parameter and array name lookup index allocatable key/state tables directly without checking the caller-supplied index range.

C entry points pass variable-length name arrays to char_array_to_string, whose dummy contract reads up to 1024 elements, so length-sized buffers without an in-range NUL can be read beyond their declared extent.
Numeric parameter getters do not verify myparam's type before reading r0 or i0, so calling a getter with a valid name of the wrong type accesses the wrong parameter component.
getcharparameter returns early on lookup failure without setting valuelength or initializing the output buffer.
Array type and rank queries return on an unknown name without initializing their output arguments.
getarraydimsize_c initializes its status to -1 and never sets it to zero after successfully computing dimsize, so every call reports failure.
Dimension-size lookup rejects only dim values greater than rank; zero or negative dimensions pass through and can reach SIZE with an invalid DIM argument, while rank-1 lookup ignores dim entirely.
Generic and rank-specific array entry points validate only the mnemonic, not that the selected array's type and rank match the routine, before dereferencing a specific pointer component.
Scalar C getters return c_loc of an unsaved local target, so the pointer becomes undefined as soon as the function returns.
Array C getters return pointers into one saved scratch allocation per rank and deallocate that allocation on the next same-rank getter call, but this short lifetime is not exposed in the API.
All C array setters convert and dereference the incoming c_ptr without checking c_associated or receiving a buffer length, so null or undersized caller buffers cannot be rejected.
Integer setters exist through rank 2 only and only ranks 0 and 1 are exposed through the module generic, while array metadata can report higher-rank integer arrays.
strlen returns zero both for an empty string and for a full 1024-byte array with no NUL terminator, so unterminated input is silently misinterpreted as empty.
strcmp constructs both string1 and string2 from char_array1, causing every comparison to report equality.
strcmp trims both converted strings and uses Fortran lexical comparison, which does not preserve ordinary C strcmp behavior for spaces preceding the NUL.
strcpy relies on the ambiguous zero returned by strlen, so an unterminated source copies only its first character and does not guarantee a terminator in the destination.
string_to_char_array does not cap len_trim to MAXSTRINGLEN-1, so strings of length 1024 or more write beyond the result when data and the terminator are stored.
string_to_char_array initializes only the payload and one terminator, leaving the remainder of its fixed 1024-element result undefined.
Module state is saved globally and init has no already-initialized guard or cleanup path, so repeated initialization can reinitialize MPI and reallocate persistent model/output state.
outputext assigns its function result only when module error is exactly 0 or 1, leaving the C-visible return value undefined for any other error code.
The optional custom timestep has neither intent nor value semantics, leaving its mutation and language-binding contract unclear to callers.
executestep sets error through timestep and skips physics on failure, but then unconditionally increments the completed-step count and returns success zero.
Output schedules and progress logging are advanced immediately after timestep reports an error, before the error guard that suppresses the physical update.
MPI finalization passes saved t01 to timing output even though t01 is assigned only when execute_counter equals 1, so short or failed runs can finalize with an undefined loop-start timestamp.
